Dated this the 17th day of August, 2020 The revision petitioner is the 1st accused in CC No.279/1997 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class -1, Thararassery and the appellant in Crl.Appeal No.536/2001 on the file of the Additional Sessions Court, Fast Track, (Adhoc-II) Kozhikode .

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional Sessions Court, Fast Track, (Adhoc-II) Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. By judgment dated 25.09.2001, the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate, Thamarassery convicted and sentenced the accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of three months and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 30 days for offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) r/w Section 2(ia)(a) and (m)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act .
Challenging the conviction and sentence, the 1 st accused preferred Criminal Appeal No.536/2001 before the Sessions Court, Kozhikode.

The learned Sessions Judge made over the case to the Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track, (Adhoc-II),
Kozhikode for hearing.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track, (Adhoc-II),
Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Additional Sessions Judge dismissed the appeal on 30.09.2005 confirming the conviction and sentence imposed by the learned magistrate.
Feeling aggrieved, the accused has preferred this Crl.Rev.Pet.No.144 OF 2006 revision.

3. The prosecution case in brief is that, on 22.01.1997 at about 3 p.m, PW1, the Food Inspector,
Kunnamangalam Circle inspected the shop room bearing No. KP 4/455 KML Gramina Oil Mills,
Pannur and purchased 450 ml of gingelly oil from the 1st accused.
The 2nd accused was the owner of the shop room and the 1st accused was conducting business therein for and on behalf of the 2 nd accused.
After complying with all legal formalities for sampling, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for report.
The Public Analyst submitted his report stating that the sample does not conform to the standard prescribed for the gingelly oil and hence adulterated.
4. Heard Sri.Sunny Mathew, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and Sri.M.S.Breez, the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. Learned counsel for the revision petitioner contended that Section 23(1)(A)(ee) and Section 23(1)(A)(hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 are violated in this case and the laboratory which issued Ext.P11 was not a defined laboratory as required under Section 23(2) of the PFA Act.

He further contended that the court below went wrong in taking cognizance under the PFA Act on the strength of Ext.P11 Form III report.
6.

In Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and Another [2010(4)KHC 767], the apex court held that in order to Crl.Rev.Pet.No.144 OF 2006 form a foundation for the prosecution after 01.04.1974, i.e., the date of incorporation of the provisions under Section 23(1)(A)(ee), the report of the public analyst must be one based on the analysis from a laboratory defined under Section 23(1)(A)(ee) following the procedure provided under Section 23(1)(A)(hh).

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. v. Food Inspector and Another [2010(4)KHC 767]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case on hand,
Ext.P11 Form III report cannot be said to be made based on an analysis conducted in such a laboratory.

7. Section 23(1), Section 23(1)(A)(ee) and Section 23(1)(A)(hh) of the PFA Act, 1954 are extracted as hereunder:-
Maniraj vs State Of Kerala on 17 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114807169/
2 "23. Power of the Central Government to make rules.-

entities.text: Maniraj vs State Of Kerala on 17 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (1) The Central Government may, after consultation with the Committee and after previous publication by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.

Provided that consultation with the Committee may be dispensed with if the Central Government is of the opinion that circumstances have arisen which render it necessary to make rules without such consultation, but, in such a case, the Committee shall be consulted within six months of the making of the rules and the Central Government shall take into consideration any suggestions which the Committee may make in relation to the amendment of the said rules.

(1-A) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power,
such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:-
xxxxxx (ee)defining the laboratories where samples of articles of food or adulterants may be analysed by public analyst under this Act xxxxxx Crl.Rev.Pet.No.144 OF 2006 (hh) defining the methods of analysis."
8.
In the light of the above, this Court is of the view that cognizance could have been taken on the complaint based on Ext.P11.
On the date of presentation of the complaint, the learned magistrate was legally prohibited from taking cognizance of the offence enumerated in the complaint,
The decision of the apex court in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd.'s case is followed by a Division Bench of this Court in Raheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery and Another [2016(2) KHC 679].

entities.text: Raheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery and Another [2016(2) KHC 679]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The apex court as well as this Court consistently held that till the repealing of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, no laboratories from where a Public Analyst to conduct analysis in terms of Section 23(1) (A)(ee) were defined.
Hence, there could not have been a report after conducting an analysis in such a laboratory defined in terms of the aforesaid provisions.

Consequently, the prosecution proceeding is liable to be terminated, for the failure to define laboratories in terms of Sections 23(1)(A)(ee) and 23(1)(A)(hh) the consequential failure to conduct an analysis of the particular sample by the Public Analyst from such a laboratory.
In the result, the revision petition is allowed.
The conviction and sentence imposed against the revision petitioner/accused stand set aside.

The revision petitioner is found not guilty for the offences punishable Crl.Rev.Pet.No.144 OF 2006 under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) r/w Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and he is acquitted for the said offences thereunder.
Cancelling his bail bond, this Court directs that he be set at liberty.

Sd/-
N.ANIL KUMAR, JUDGE dlk/06.08.2020 Maniraj vs State Of Kerala on 17 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114807169/
